title: microprobe-operator-manifest-and-sampling-economics-playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Title: Microprobe Operator Manifest and Sampling Economics Playbook

Summary
-------
This playbook defines the Microprobe Operator (MPO): a lightweight runtime component and operational pattern for high-signal, low-cost instrumentation inside the Redwood serving runtime. The MPO is intended for short-duration probes that diagnose kernel-level behavior, KV-cache warmup characteristics, and burst-tail latency without blowing observability budgets or perturbing production scheduling.

Purpose and scope
------------------
- Purpose: Provide a repeatable contract and operational playbook for introducing, tuning, and retiring microprobes across the runtime surface.
- Scope: In-process and sidecar probes that run on serving nodes (GPU hosts and inference routers). Not intended for deep kernel modifications or external end-to-end tracing frameworks.
- Audience: runtime engineers, profiler owners, oncall SREs, and experimenters.

Ownership and stakeholders
-------------------------
- MPO owner: runtime-profiling team (team contact: @priya).
- Observability integration: telemetry-adapters team (reviewer: Daniel Wu).
- Scheduling/Kernel impact review: kernel-scheduler team (reviewer: Marco Alvarez).
- Release gate: must pass profiling lab acceptance criteria (see Benchmarks section).

Design principles
------------------
1. Non-invasive: probes must avoid long-lived locks or changes to scheduler behavior.
2. Budgeted: every probe is assigned a fixed cost budget (CPU ms, bytes emitted, average frequency).
3. Lightweight sampling: prefer probabilistic micro-sampling over continuous tracing.
4. Amortize work: aggregate telemetry at the operator boundary and send compacted summaries.
5. Kill-switchable: MPOs must honor a single operator-level remote flag for immediate global disablement.

Microprobe operator architecture
-------------------------------
- Components:
  - Controller (central): issues probe manifests and budgets via ConfigStore.
  - Agent (node-level MPO): receives manifests, enforces local budgets, collects samples, and emits compressed summaries.
  - Exporter: adapts compressed summaries to the telemetry pipeline and decides real-time vs batched ingestion.

Probe types
-----------
1. Touch probes: measure cold-start wall time of model shard activation (100-200ms probe).
2. Kernel rendezvous probes: sample kernel launch latencies and kernel queue lengths during busy windows.
3. KV-cache sweep probes: light samplers that touch a small prefix/slot distribution to estimate hit rates.
4. Tail request microtraces: capture 1-in-N full traces for requests above a latency threshold.

Budgeting and economics (mandatory fields)
-----------------------------------------
Each probe manifest contains a table of required budget fields. Operators must supply limits before activation.

Table: Probe budget schema (CSV-like)
probe_id,owner,probe_type,cpu_budget_ms_per_min,node_emit_bytes_per_min,max_sample_rate_per_min,ttl_minutes,backoff_policy
mp-touch-01,priya,touch,200,50000,20,60,exponential
mp-kernel-queue-01,marco,kernel-rendezvous,500,120000,10,30,linear
mp-kv-sweep-01,analytics,kv-sweep,150,30000,30,120,exponential
mp-tailtrace-rare-01,sre,tail-trace,1000,500000,2,1440,manual

Sampling policy and heuristics
-----------------------------
- Default mode: budgeted probabilistic sampling. Node agent maintains a leaky-bucket counter per-probe.
- Threshold triggers: probes may be promoted to higher fidelity if a health rule fires (e.g., rising tail latency > 99th percentile threshold).
- Reservoir caps: maximum number of retained microtraces kept in memory (default 32 per node).
- Backoff behaviors: exponential backoff when emission errors > 5% for 2 consecutive minutes.

Operational lifecycle (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------
1. Draft manifest: profiling owner prepares probe manifest with budgets and rationale.
2. Risk review: submit to kernel-scheduler and telemetry-adapters for capacity and perturbation review.
3. Canary rollout (week-long): enable MPO at 1% of serving fleet with debug-level local sampling, validate no scheduler jitter.
4. Acceptance: run the profiling-lab acceptance checklist and cost simulation (see Benchmarks).
5. Production rollout: ramp to target fraction with progressive budget tightening.
6. Retention and sunset: every probe must include a sunset_date or a quarterly review ticket.

Deployment checklist
---------------------
- Manifest fields populated: probe_id, owner, budgets, safe-mode flag, TTL.
- Canary matrix defined: which clusters, node classes, and models.
- Observability: metrics defined (probe_success_rate, emit_errors, budget_utilization).
- Kill-switch validated end-to-end.

Runbook: probe-overload incident (short)
---------------------------------------
1. Symptoms:
   - sudden spike in exporter queue length or telemetry pipeline backpressure metrics.
   - increased scheduler soft-evictions during probe windows.
2. Immediate actions:
   1. Trigger MPO global kill-switch via ConfigStore.
   2. Identify offending probe_id using controller logs and budget_utilization panel.
   3. Notify probe owner and kernel-scheduler oncall.
3. Recovery:
   - After kill, verify exporter queues drain and scheduler quota stabilizes for 10 minutes.
   - If safe, re-enable in canary with 10x tighter budget and monitoring.

Benchmarks and acceptance criteria
----------------------------------
- CPU overhead: < 0.5% average CPU across probes in steady state (measured on target node class).
- Telemetry volume: < 1.5% of total telemetry bytes for active probes in aggregate.
- Perturbation: no measurable increase (>1%) in 95th percentile latency for the canary cohort.
- Safety: killing MPO must restore baseline within 2 minutes.

Measurement harness (how to verify)
----------------------------------
1. Use the profiling harness: ./tools/probe-harness --manifest <manifest.yaml> --simulate-workload <trace.json>
2. Collect metrics from MPO dashboards: probe_success_rate, budget_utilization, exporter_queue_ms.
3. Run A/B: mirror 10% of traffic to a shadow node with MPO enabled and compare latency histograms.

Configuration examples
----------------------
YAML manifest example (compact):

---
probe_id: mp-kv-sweep-01
owner: analytics
probe_type: kv-sweep
cpu_budget_ms_per_min: 150
node_emit_bytes_per_min: 30000
max_sample_rate_per_min: 30
ttl_minutes: 120
backoff_policy: exponential
kill_switch_flag: /config/probes/enabled
telemetry_targets: ["compact-summary", "rare-full-trace"]
---

CLI examples (agent)
--------------------
- List active manifests: rwd-mpoctl list --env prod --cluster west-gpu
- Force kill: rwd-mpoctl kill mp-kv-sweep-01 --reason "emitter-backpressure"
- Drain and archive: rwd-mpoctl drain mp-tailtrace-rare-01 --archive-to s3://redwood-probe-archives/

Telemetry contract (what MPO emits)
------------------------------------
- Compact summary (default): gzipped protobuf containing aggregated counters, 95/99 latency summaries, small histograms.
- Rare full trace: sampled full trace with kernel IDs and microsecond timestamps (reserved for tail traces).
- Emission envelope must include probe_id, sample_timestamp, node_id, and budget_consumed.

Appendix: safe experiment template (copy-paste)
------------------------------------------------
1) Experiment name: <owner>-<probe_id>-<date>
2) Hypothesis: short 1–2 sentence statement.
3) Canaries: cluster / node-class list and expected ramp.
4) Budget table: include CPU and bytes.
5) Success criteria: latency windows, telemetry quota, no-sd.
6) Rollback plan: immediate kill-switch + postmortem owner.

Notes and cautions
------------------
- Microprobes are powerful but can create subtle feedback with the scheduler; always use the lab harness before production rollout.
- Never increase sample rates in production without kernel-scheduler signoff when running on preemptible node classes.
